key_insight: APRIL-MedSeg is a modular, YAML-driven toolbox that makes 2D medical image segmentation easier to build, reuse, and extend. It unifies many modern segmentation paradigms—like semi-supervised learning, domain adaptation, distillation, weak supervision, and text-guided methods—under one framework.
problem_solved: Medical image segmentation research is often fragmented across many custom codebases, making it hard to reproduce results, compare methods fairly, or combine advanced training paradigms. This paper addresses the need for a unified, extensible system that simplifies experimentation and integration.
method: Decomposes segmentation models into reusable modules for backbone, decoder, loss, and training strategy components.
Uses a YAML-driven configuration and registry system with inheritance to quickly assemble and customize experiments.

Supports multiple modern paradigms in one framework, including semi-supervised, domain adaptation, knowledge distillation, weak supervision, text-guided segmentation, and foundation-model-based workflows.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, APRIL-MedSeg reduces engineering overhead and accelerates experimentation in medical image segmentation. It also improves reproducibility and makes it easier to benchmark and combine emerging methods in a consistent way.
visual_elements: A modular pipeline diagram showing interchangeable model components
A YAML configuration flowchart illustrating inheritance and registry-based setup
An ecosystem map of supported paradigms (semi-supervised, domain adaptation, distillation, etc.)
A before-vs-after comparison of fragmented codebases versus a unified toolbox
paper_title: APRIL-MedSeg: A Modular Medical Image Segmentation Toolbox Embracing Modern Paradigms
paper_authors: Juntao Jiang, Jinsheng Bai, Linxuan Fan, Yali Bi, Jiangning Zhang
